the Pan American Games|Pan American Games]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games|2015 Toronto]] | }} }} '''Andrew Fabian Nicholson''' (born December 8, 1989) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Seoul Samsung Thunders]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure Bonnies]] before being selected by the [[Orlando Magic]] with the 19th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Nicholson did not start playing until he was a high school junior. Due to a broken [[ankle]], he missed the entire summer circuit prior to his senior season. Nicholson gained recognition in his senior and 5th year. He was named to the ''[[Toronto Star]]'' High School All-Stars in 2007 and 2008, and was also named [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] of five different tournaments.{{cite web | url = http://areyouwatchingthis.com/ncaab/news/208274-St-Bonaventures-Nicholson-becoming-extraordinary | title = St. Bonaventure's Nicholson becoming extraordinary | work = areyouwatchingthis.com | date = November 19, 2010 | access-date = December 21, 2014}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2008}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Andrew Nicholson | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Mississauga, ON]] | highschool = [[Father Michael Goetz Secondary School]] (ON) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 250 | 40 = | commitdate = October 17, 2007 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 2 | espn grade = 40 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2008 | rivals ref title = St. Bonaventure 2008 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2008 St. Bonaventure Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = | rivals overall = | espn overall = | accessdate = April 9, 2012 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== As a freshman at [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]] in 2008–09, Nicholson earned Atlantic 10 Rookie of the Year honours after winning the A-10 Rookie of the Week award a program record six times. He also earned ''CollegeHoopsNet.com'' Freshman All-American team honours. He made 25 starts out of 30 games played and led all freshmen nationally in field goal percentage (.602) and blocks (81). He averaged 12.5 points and 6.0 rebounds in 25.1 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=44 - Andrew Nicholson |url=http://gobonnies.sbu.edu/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/bios/nicholson_andrew00.html |url-status=dead |access-date=December 21, 2014 |work=GoBonnies.sbu.edu |archive-date=December 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221205935/http://gobonnies.sbu.edu/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/bios/nicholson_andrew00.html }} ===Sophomore year=== As a sophomore in 2009–10, Nicholson earned second-team All-Atlantic 10 honours after starting all 30 games and averaging 16.4 points and 7.1 rebounds in 30.2 minutes per game. He ranked 18th nationally, and second in the A-10, in field goal percentage at .564 (198–351), the ninth-best season total in program history. He scored a season-high 29 points on two separate occasions, the first of which came on 11-of-13 shooting from the floor with a career-best 14 rebounds against [[Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball|Norfolk State]] on November 28; second came at [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] on January 23, where he played the full 40 minutes. ===Junior year=== As a junior in 2010–11, Nicholson was an Atlantic 10 Preseason and All-Defensive first team selection, and went on to earn first-team All-Atlantic 10 and first-team NABC All-District honours. He also earned Atlantic 10 Co-Player of the Week for the week of December 20 with eventual conference Player of the Year [[Tu Holloway]]. He became the 38th player in school history to surpass the 1,000-point barrier with a foul-line jumper in the first half of the Niagara game on December 11, 2010.{{Cite web |last=Skurski |first=Jay |date=November 10, 2011 |title=SPREADING HIS WINGS; High-scoring big man Andrew Nicholson has put St. Bonaventure on his shoulders and carried it back to basketball respectability |url=https://buffalonews.com/news/spreading-his-wings-high-scoring-big-man-andrew-nicholson-has-put-st-bonaventure-on-his/article_ef702dde-79fa-544a-9f41-5e24d7171710.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=buffalonews.com}} In 31 games (all starts), he averaged 20.8 points and 7.3 rebounds in 33.8 minutes per game. He scored a career-high 44 points, on 14-of-19 field goals and 16-of-25 from the free throw line, while pulling down 12 rebounds in a four-overtime thriller against Ohio on December 18, the longest game in SBU history. ===Senior year=== As a senior in 2011–12, Nicholson earned Atlantic 10 Player of the Year honours in addition to All-American Honorable Mention, and first-team All-Atlantic 10 and All-Defensive team honours. He became the seventh player in the 35-year history of the league to earn both Rookie and Player of the Year honours and the first St. Bonaventure Bonnie to earn the top overall award since [[Earl Belcher]] won two in a row in 1980 and 1981. He also became the first player in the history of the league to earn four straight Player of the Week awards. He scored his 2,000th career point and averaged a [[double-double]] in the final week of the season, posting 25.5 points and 11.0 rebounds. In 32 games (all starts), he averaged 18.5 points and 8.4 rebounds in 30.1 minutes per game. He finished his four-year career at St. Bonaventure with 2,103 points, 887 rebounds and 244 blocks in 123 games (118 starts). ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" web|url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/games/20120709/BKNORL/gameinfo.html|title=Summer League: Magic 92, Nets 88|last=John|first=Denton|date=July 9, 2012|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2012}} web|url=http://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2012/12/21/3793020/glen-davis-injury-andrew-nicholson-start-orlando-magic-toronto-raptors|title=Andrew Nicholson replaces injured Glen Davis for Magic Rising Stars game |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/2/10/3974214/andrew-nicholson-to-replace-andre-drummond-in-rising-stars-game |access-date=July 8, 2016 |website=sbnation.com}} ====2013–14 season==== In July 2013, Nicholson re-joined the Magic for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On October 26, 2013, the Magic exercised their third-year team option on Nicholson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2014–15 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-exercise-contract-options-harkless-harris-nicholson-and-vucevic|title=Magic Exercise Contract Options on Harkless, Harris, Nicholson and Vucevic|work=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2013|access-date=December 21, 2014}} He scored in double figures in 11 of the first 23 games, including three double-doubles. However, following the December 13 game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Nicholson managed just four more double-figure-scoring games and finished the season averaging 5.7 points and 3.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/nichoan01/gamelog/2014/| title = Andrew Nicholson 2013-14 Game Log| work = Basketball-Reference.com| access-date = December 21, 2014}} ====2014–15 season==== On October 26, 2014, the Magic exercised their fourth-year team option on Nicholson's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/magic-exercise-contract-options-fournier-harkless-nicholson-and-oladipo|title=Magic Exercise Contract Options on Fournier, Harkless, Nicholson and Oladipo|work=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2014|access-date=December 21, 2014}} Nicholson spent most of the 2014–15 season out of the team's playing rotation. He didn't play in 38 of the Magic's first 56 games even though he was injury free, but playing time increased significantly after the All-Star break. He appeared in 22 of Orlando's final 26 games and averaged 15.1 minutes, 6.3 points and 2.6 rebounds per game over that 22-game stretch.{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/magic-basketblog/os-mbb-andrew-nicholson-orlando-magic-evaluation-20150507-post.html|title=Evaluating Andrew Nicholson's 2014-15 season|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=May 7, 2015|access-date=December 9, 2015}} Overall, he averaged 4.9 points and 2.1 rebounds in 40 games. ====2015–16 season==== After appearing in just two of the Magic's first 11 games to start the 2015–16 season, Nicholson began to pick up game time and production from November 18 onwards. On November 23, 2015, Nicholson scored a season-high 18 points and 8 rebounds in a loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2015 |title=LeBron leads Cavs past Magic, joins Robertson on elite list |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400828090 |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On December 8, 2015, he recorded 8 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in an 85–74 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |date=December 8, 2015 |title=Vucevic leads Magic to 85-74 win over Nuggets |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151208/ORLDEN/gameinfo.html
